briefTitle: Suzetrigine Following Urogynecologic Surgery: Investigation of Postoperative Pain Management
officialTitle: Suzetrigine Following Urogynecologic Surgery: Investigation of Postoperative Pain Management

arms.label: Experimental Group
arms.description: Participants will receive suzetrigine 100 mg (2 tablets) as a loading dose on the evening of surgery, followed by 50 mg every 12 hours for 7 days, in addition to standard multimodal analgesia. Standard analgesia consists of ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours and acetaminophen 650 mg every 6 hours, scheduled for the first 48 hours postoperatively, after which patients may transition to as-needed dosing of both. An opioid prescription will be sent if triggered by previously set score and based on the patient's reported pain score.

arms.label: Control Group
arms.description: Participants will receive matching placebo as a loading dose (2 tablets) on the evening of surgery, followed by 1 tablet every 12 hours for 7 days, in addition to standard multimodal analgesia. Standard analgesia consists of ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours and acetaminophen 650 mg every 6 hours, scheduled for the first 48 hours postoperatively, after which patients may transition to as-needed dosing of both. An opioid prescription will be sent if triggered by the patient's reported pain score.

eligibility.text:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Women ≥ 40 years and ≤ 80
* BMI \>=18.0 and \<= 40.0
* Can read and speak English or Spanish
* Undergoing major urogynecologic surgery, defined as having at least one of the following:

  * Robotic-assisted laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy
  * Uterosacral ligament suspension (laparoscopic or vaginal approach)
  * Uterosacral hysteropexy
  * Sacrospinous hysteropexy
  * Sacrospinous ligament fixation
  * Conversion to laparotomy during primary surgery for prolapse repair

Exclusion Criteria:

* • Current narcotic use defined as daily use for more than 7 consecutive days in the 3 months prior to surgery, or current treatment for opioid use disorder.

  * Any opioid use within 30 days prior to the scheduled procedure date.
  * Significant hepatic disease, defined as AST or ALT \>3 times the upper limit of normal or Child-Pugh class B or C.
  * Diagnosis of chronic pain syndrome or fibromyalgia
  * Inability to provide written informed consent
  * History of significant respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, neurologic, or psychiatric disease as deemed clinically significant by study team
  * History of cardiac dysrhythmias requiring anti-arrhythmia treatment(s) within the last 2 years or QT prolongation (QTcF \>450 ms) or pacemaker/ICD
  * Severe kidney disease define as Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of ≤ 30ml/min
  * Inability to receive or respond to text messages via mobile phone
  * Receives transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block
  * Allergy to any of the study medications
  * Use of moderate or strong CYP3A inducers or inhibitors, including prescription medications, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements known to significantly affect CYP3A metabolism (e.g., ketoconazole, clarithromycin, rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, ritonavir, and St. John's Wort).
  * Pregnant or breastfeeding or planning to become pregnant within 30 days following last dose of study drug
